sections.heading: What are Qualifying Cutoff and Allotment Cutoff?

items: Qualifying Cutoff or BAMS cutoff for NEET 2025 is the minimum score required in the NEET examination to be eligible to participate in the Ayush counselling for BAMS admission in Karnataka .

Seat Allotment Cutoff is the minimum score required for securing a seat in a specific BAMS college. The seat allotment cutoff differs based on the category of the candidates and the allotted quota. For each round, KEA releases the seat allotment cutoff with opening and closing ranks.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
Can I get BAMS with 250 marks in NEET?

content.text: It may be challenging to get BAMS with 250 marks in NEET in the government colleges. You will have a higher chance of admission to private colleges with your marks.

sections.heading: What is the BAMS cutoff in Karnataka for OBC?

content.text: The BAMS cutoff in Karnataka for OBC category in 2025 is 143-113.

sections.heading: What are the marks required for BAMS government college?

content.text: Generally, a score from 450- 500 is the marks required for BAMS government colleges.

sections.heading: What is the BAMS NEET cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category?

content.text: The BAMS NEET cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category is 143-113.

sections.heading: How many marks are required in NEET for BAMS?

content.text: The marks required in NEET for BAMS are generally from 450- 500 in government colleges and 350-450 in private colleges. The marks required in both government and private colleges are much lower for the reserved category.

sections.heading: Are management quota seats available for BAMS admission in Karnataka?

content.text: Yes, private colleges in Karnataka offer BAMS admission under the Management quota.

sections.heading: Can I get BAMS admission with low NEET score?

content.text: You have a higher chance of admission with low NEET score in private BAMS colleges under the management quota.

sections.heading: What is the seat allotment cutoff?

content.text: The seat allotment cutoff is the minimum required marks published during the counselling to get into specific BAMS colleges. The cutoff varies between colleges in the same state.

What are Qualifying Cutoff and Allotment Cutoff?

Qualifying Cutoff or BAMS cutoff for NEET 2025 is the minimum score required in the NEET examination to be eligible to participate in the Ayush counselling for BAMS admission in Karnataka .

Seat Allotment Cutoff is the minimum score required for securing a seat in a specific BAMS college. The seat allotment cutoff differs based on the category of the candidates and the allotted quota. For each round, KEA releases the seat allotment cutoff with opening and closing ranks.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I get BAMS with 250 marks in NEET?

It may be challenging to get BAMS with 250 marks in NEET in the government colleges. You will have a higher chance of admission to private colleges with your marks.

What is the BAMS cutoff in Karnataka for OBC?

The BAMS cutoff in Karnataka for OBC category in 2025 is 143-113.

What are the marks required for BAMS government college?

Generally, a score from 450- 500 is the marks required for BAMS government colleges.

What is the BAMS NEET cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category?

The BAMS NEET cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category is 143-113.

How many marks are required in NEET for BAMS?

The marks required in NEET for BAMS are generally from 450- 500 in government colleges and 350-450 in private colleges. The marks required in both government and private colleges are much lower for the reserved category.

Are management quota seats available for BAMS admission in Karnataka?

Yes, private colleges in Karnataka offer BAMS admission under the Management quota.

Can I get BAMS admission with low NEET score?

You have a higher chance of admission with low NEET score in private BAMS colleges under the management quota.

What is the seat allotment cutoff?

The seat allotment cutoff is the minimum required marks published during the counselling to get into specific BAMS colleges. The cutoff varies between colleges in the same state.
